title: Patient Financial Services Terms: Hardship Application Postings in the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Ship-Time Past-Due Test
content:
Patient financial services terms — Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program, Larkfield Medical Supply.

## 1. The ship-time past-due test

For the ship-time past-due test of the refill count for a sensor refill (A4239) delivery drawing on the authorization grant resting on the newest written order of the item, on a tier where each refill requires the customer's own confirmation, and of the plan member waiver count, and only for that test, a posting counts as past due once the whole calendar months given by the tier's past-due age in days divided by 30, rounded down, have passed from its posting date to today; no posting counts on a tier whose past-due age is 0; the past-due remittance patient responsibility, other than a posting named on a hardship application, counts as covered while an approved payment plan's installments are current; and a posting named on a hardship application is set aside as section 2 of these terms states. Every program hold for a past-due balance still rests on the past-due balance hold condition: on tiers where the past-due age is greater than 0, the program's past-due amount is at least the tier's past-due hold minimum and no approved payment plan covers it.

## 2. A posting under a hardship application

A posting under a hardship application is set aside by taking it off the program's past-due amount, by these rules, reading the latest hardship application on the program (the one most recently logged) and the posting it names:

| Latest hardship application on the program | What is taken off the past-due amount |
|---|---|
| names a posting and is still awaiting decision | that posting's whole amount is taken off |
| names a posting and is approved | that posting's amount less the balance adjustments posted against that posting is taken off |
| otherwise: denied, completed or withdrawn, or no hardship application on the program | nothing is taken off |

Only the latest hardship application counts; an earlier application on the program sets nothing aside, whatever its status. An application that names no posting sets nothing aside under any status, since there is no posting amount to take.

## 3. Customer questions answered by these terms

- A customer whose hardship application is still awaiting decision asks whether the posting it names counts in the past-due amount. It does not: the whole amount of that posting is taken off the past-due amount.
- A customer whose application was approved asks what still counts. Once approved, only the part of the named posting that the balance adjustments posted against it have not cleared is taken off; balance adjustments posted against other postings do not reduce the amount set aside.
- A customer whose application was denied asks the same question. Nothing is set aside; the named posting counts like any other.

## 4. Illustration (hypothetical amounts)

Suppose the latest hardship application on a program names a remittance patient responsibility posting of 200.00 USD, and a hardship-waiver balance adjustment of 150.00 USD has posted against that posting.

- While the application is awaiting decision: 200.00 is taken off the past-due amount.
- Once it is approved: 200.00 less 150.00, that is 50.00, is taken off.
- If it is denied: nothing is taken off.
